skill.name: lottie
skill.description: Lottie and dotLottie adapter patterns for HyperFrames. Use when embedding lottie-web JSON animations, .lottie files, @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web players, registering instances on window.__hfLottie, or making After Effects exports deterministic in HyperFrames.
skill.summary: Embed lottie-web and dotLottie animations in HyperFrames with deterministic player registration.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, fenced examples, and inline code labels in SKILL.md. The real residual risk is low: two examples load third-party Lottie player scripts from public CDNs, while the remaining URLs are documentation references. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer locally vendored, version-pinned Lottie player assets. If a CDN is required, document trust requirements and use integrity checks where supported.

remediation.issue: External validation commands are shown in the skill
remediation.suggestion: Keep validation commands fixed and project-scoped. Agents should request user approval before running npx commands in untrusted repositories.

static_findings.snippet: HyperFrames can seek both `lottie-web` and dotLottie players through its `lottie` runtime adapter. L
- Load assets from local project files, usually under `assets/`.
- Prefer `loop: false` unless the user explicitly wants a loop.
- Register every returned animation or player on `window.__hfLottie`.
The adapter seeks `lottie-web` with `goToAndStop(timeMs, false)` and dotLottie with frame or percent
- Relying on remote `path` URLs at render time.
- Assuming unsupported After Effects effects will survive export. Test the JSON or `.lottie` file in
- dotLottie web player methods by LottieFiles: https://developers.lottiefiles.com/docs/dotlottie-pla

content.value_statement: HyperFrames Lottie scenes need consistent player setup, local assets, and reliable timeline seeking. This skill provides lottie-web and dotLottie patterns that register players and keep validation predictable.
actual_capabilities: Shows a lottie-web setup using a local animation asset and disabled autoplay.
Shows a dotLottie canvas setup using a local .lottie asset and disabled looping.
Explains how to register animation players on the shared window.__hfLottie registry.
Describes how multiple animations can be synchronized by HyperFrames.
Provides validation steps for linting and validating a HyperFrames composition.
limitations: It does not create or repair Lottie animation files.
It assumes the project uses the HyperFrames lottie runtime adapter.
It uses CDN script examples that may need local replacements for locked-down builds.
It cannot guarantee unsupported After Effects effects will export correctly.

best_practices: Use local animation assets instead of remote render-time paths.
Disable autoplay and looping unless the scene explicitly requires looping.
Register every player before HyperFrames validation inspects the page.
anti_patterns: Loading animation JSON from remote URLs during render.
Calling player playback methods instead of relying on HyperFrames seeking.
Changing container dimensions during animation playback.

faq.question: Does this skill generate Lottie animation files?
faq.answer: No. It helps embed existing lottie-web JSON and dotLottie files in HyperFrames.

faq.question: Can I use remote animation assets?
faq.answer: The skill recommends local assets for deterministic rendering and fewer network dependencies.

faq.question: Why should autoplay be disabled?
faq.answer: HyperFrames controls time by seeking players. Autoplay can make renders non-deterministic.

faq.question: How are multiple animations synchronized?
faq.answer: Each player is registered in the shared HyperFrames Lottie registry, then HyperFrames seeks them together.

faq.question: Does it support lottie-web and dotLottie?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes separate patterns for lottie-web JSON and dotLottie canvas playback.

faq.question: What should I test before rendering?
faq.answer: Test the exported animation in a browser, then run HyperFrames lint and validation.
